An ecocritical reading of a literary text is, simply, one which in some way incorporates a consideration of the kind of issues and concerns we have just been discussing. But there is, as we have said, no universally accepted model that we have merely to learn and apply. Often, it is just a matter of approaching perhaps very familiar texts with a new alertness to this dimension, a dimension which has perhaps always hovered about the text, but without ever receiving our full attention before. This is well illustrated in the opening of a short piece by Ralph W. Black entitled ‘What we talk about when we talk about ecocriticism’:

不久前，我又看了一遍《李尔王》。奥利弗版的《李尔王》。我像往常一样，为李尔王深沉的愤怒和更深沉的悲伤所震撼，也像往常一样，在他最后抱着科迪莉亚的尸体走过舞台时，我潸然泪下。但更让我震撼的是开场：一幅王国地图展开，绘制在一小群皇家鹿的鞣制皮毛上。老君主用剑象征性地将他的领土分给他的女儿们。甚至在女儿们开口讲述（或拒绝讲述）她们爱情的轨迹之前，这种越轨行为就已经发生了：这片商品化的土地被切割分割，卖给了出价最高的雄辩家。那一刻，我开始思考自己对这部悲剧的理解，思考究竟是什么样的傲慢行为导致了李尔王的陨落，思考自然世界在剧中的意义，思考那些似乎都发生在户外——暴风雨中、荒原上、海边——的清醒时刻。6

Not long ago I saw King Lear again. Olivier’s Lear. I marvelled as usual at Lear’s deep rage and deeper sadness, and I cried as usual as he carried Cordelia’s body across the stage at the end. But I was struck even more by the beginning: A map of the kingdom is unrolled. It is painted across the tanned hides of a small herd of royal deer. The old Sovereign uses his sword to symbolically divide his domain among his daughters. Even before the daughters have spoken, or refused to speak, the trajectory of their love, there is this transgression: the commodified landscape is sliced up and parcelled out to the highest rhetorical bidder. For a moment I wonder about my understanding of the tragedy, about what hubristic act instigates Lear’s fall, about the significance of the natural world in the play, the moments of clarity that all seem to take place outside – in a storm, on the moors, at the seashore.6

这些引言预示着一种与以往任何解读都截然不同的《李尔王》解读方式，这并非因为该剧被简化为生态考量，而是因为生态考量首次被纳入到以往传统解读中所有其他议题的考量之中。这种解读会提醒我们，科迪莉亚所能获得的王国份额（“第三富裕的份额”），只要她言行一致，便是真实存在的有人居住的土地——山丘、田野、河流、农场、村落——而这些土地即将被君主随意分割，仿佛它们本身没有任何权利或完整性。同样，李尔王发疯的“荒芜之地”也是这片领土内真实存在的地方，或许它（以其“荒芜”之感）象征着这片土地因李尔王的行为而遭受的政治后果——忽视和衰败。这场风暴不仅是李尔王疯狂的象征，也是真实的天气，代表着他反常行为所拒绝面对的自然进程，例如他自身的衰老，以及由此导致的被下一代边缘化（托尔斯泰说：“所有老人都是李尔王”）。弗洛伊德也认为《李尔王》是典型的“家庭剧”。因此，对经典文本的生态批评解读，首先要加入不同的视角，而不仅仅局限于那些显而易见地与自然有关的作品。

These introductory remarks signal a reading of Lear which would have a distinctly different flavour from any other, not because the play is being reduced to ecological considerations, but, rather, because these are being added for the first time to all the other issues which more traditional approaches have always seen in the play. Such a reading would remind us that the slice of the kingdom available to Cordelia (the ‘third more opulent’), provided she says what her father wants to hear, is real peopled landscape – hills, fields, rivers, farms, communities – which are about to be randomly chopped up at the monarch’s whim, as if they had no claims or integrity of their own. Likewise, the ‘blasted heath’ on which Lear enacts his madness is a real place located somewhere within this territory, and perhaps emblematic (in its ‘blastedness’) of the neglect and degradation which that territory suffers as a political consequence of Lear’s act. The storm, too, isn’t just the emblematic correlative of Lear’s madness, but real weather, representing the natural processes which his unnatural behaviour refuses to come to terms with, processes such as his own aging, and his consequent side-lining by the following generation (‘All old men are King Lear’, said Tolstoy, and Freud, too, saw Lear as an archetypal ‘family drama’). Ecocritical readings of canonical texts, then, begin by adding a different perspective, and are not limited to works self-evidently about nature.

但这里所指的《李尔王》解读还有另一个值得特别注意的特点，那就是它颠覆了传统的阅读方式（姑且这么说）。这意味着它的策略似乎是将批评的注意力从内在转向外在，从而将原本看似仅仅是“背景”的东西从批评的边缘带到了批评的中心（这样一来，风暴就变成了真正的风暴，而不仅仅是李尔王内心动荡的隐喻）。我想用另一篇文本作为例子，更详细地阐述这一重要的转变——这种拒绝将内在置于外在之上的做法，目的是强调这并非一种简化，而是丰富了我们文学研究的生命之源——复杂性，而不是削弱了它。我在这里使用的文本是埃德加·爱伦·坡的著名小说《厄舍府的倒塌》。7在故事中，罗德里克·厄舍和他的妹妹玛德琳自愿被囚禁在古老、破败、孤寂的厄舍府中。这座府邸毗邻一个阴森恐怖的湖泊，“一个漆黑阴森的小湖，静静地躺在府邸旁，波光粼粼”。妹妹患有一种奇怪的消耗性疾病，而厄舍本人，一个“崇高而精神理想化”的人，却饱受“感官异常敏锐”的折磨，这使他无法忍受与自然界的任何接触——“所有花香都令他感到压抑；即使是微弱的光线也会让他的眼睛痛苦不堪”。他与外界的唯一联系是通过艺术。当叙述者第一次见到他时，“许多书籍和乐器散落在各处，却未能给这景象增添任何生机。”

But the Lear reading implied here does have one other characteristic which is worth noting particularly, namely the way it tends to turn the conventional manner of reading inside out (so to speak). By this is meant that its strategy seems to be to switch critical attention from inner to outer, so that what had seemed mere ‘setting’ is brought in from the critical margins to the critical centre (so that, among other things, the storm is a storm, and not just a metaphor for the turmoil in Lear’s mind). I want to illustrate this important move – this refusal to privilege the inner over the outer – at slightly greater length using another text as example, the aim being to emphasise that this need not be a reductive move, and that the complexity which is (after all) the life-blood of our literary study is thereby enriched rather than diluted. The text I am using here is Edgar Allan Poe’s well-known tale ‘The Fall of the House of Usher’.7 In the tale, Roderick Usher and his sister Madeline undergo a kind of voluntary imprisonment in the ancient, crumbling, isolated House of Usher, which stands next to an evil-looking lake, ‘a black and lurid tarn that lay in unruffled lustre by the dwelling’. The sister suffers from a strange wasting disease, while Usher himself, a being of ‘lofty and spiritual ideality’, is afflicted by ‘a morbid acuteness of the senses’, which makes him unable to bear any contact with the natural world – ‘the odours of all flowers were oppressive; his eyes were tortured by even a faint light’. His only contact with the world beyond himself is through art, and when the narrator first encounters him, ‘many books and musical instruments lay scattered about, but failed to give any vitality to the scene.’

这篇故事通常着重解读厄舍府的病态心理，以及叙述者的到来如何以一种奇异的方式引发了玛德琳的衰落：叙述者参与了将她过早地埋葬在他房间正下方的地窖中，并精心策划了她的再次出现（他大声朗读给……听）。（出自一部耸人听闻的小说，其情节与下方正在上演的怪诞的越狱与复活的戏剧性事件遥相呼应。）目睹复活的妹妹玛德琳的惊吓夺去了患有神经衰弱的厄舍的生命。由于所有这些事件都由未具名的叙述者引发，因此人们通常将厄舍和玛德琳解读为叙述者自身存在的不同面向，即他理性思维的潜意识层面。这是一种常见的文学批评手法——将外部因素（无论是人物、物品、情境还是事件）解读为内部因素（在本例中，即潜意识的组成部分）。

The tale is usually read with a focus on the morbid psychology of Usher, and on the strange way in which the narrator’s arrival triggers Madeline’s decline: the narrator’s complicity in her premature entombment in the vault directly beneath his own room is described, as well as his orchestration of her re-appearance (he reads aloud to Usher from a lurid novel which parallels the grotesque drama of break-out and resurgence taking place below). The shock of seeing his resurrected sister kills the neurasthenic Usher, and because the presence of the unnamed narrator triggers all these events, it is common to read Usher and Madeline as aspects of the narrator’s own being, that is, as the subconscious underside of his rationality. This is a common literary-critical ploy – the external (whether characters, objects, situations, or events) is read as internal (in this case, as elements of the subconscious).

与之相反，以生态为中心的解读则将焦点放在房屋及其周围环境上，而非房屋内部的主人及其心理状态。它运用了能量、熵（一种系统内部的负能量，趋向于崩溃和混乱）以及共生（“共生”字面意思是“共同生活”，指相互维持、共存的系统）等概念。因此，房屋被视为一个孤立的熵系统，与更广阔的生物圈没有任何共生联系。死寂的湖面映照着房屋自身静止的影像；房屋吸入了自身衰败的气息——“一种围绕着水面和墙壁逐渐​​而确定地凝结成自身特有的氛围”。它拥有自己封闭的小气候，随着高潮临近，它似乎在自身被禁锢和扼杀的能量中煎熬。当厄舍府和叙述者向窗外望去时，“浓密的云层（低垂到几乎压在房屋的塔楼上）也未能阻止我们感知到它们如同生命般飞舞的速度，它们从四面八方涌来，彼此碰撞，却始终没有消散到远方”。因此，厄舍府并非一个生命系统的一部分；没有新的元素从外部注入能量，使其能够融入其他系统；它是一盏熄灭的灯，一条断流的溪流，一团无火可燃的火焰。它自恋地疏离于更广阔的生命力流动之外，使它变成了一个黑洞，最终化作一个漩涡，将自身的能量吸入其中，最终毁灭——正如叙述者望向窗外时所说，“一股旋风似乎在我们附近聚集了它的力量”。此外，我们还能看到房子最终坍塌并消失的黑色水潭（或湖泊）。最令人毛骨悚然的莫过于厄舍的内心，“黑暗仿佛一种内在的积极特质，从中倾泻而出，笼罩着一切道德和物质的事物。”宇宙，在永无止境的阴郁辐射中。因此，厄舍尔散发的不是能量，而是熵，如同即将坍缩的恒星奔向自身的瓦解。令人恐惧的是，他完全是“文化”的化身，而与“自然”毫无关联；他“畏光”（对光线极其敏感），完全无法忍受自然光，只偏爱绘画中呈现的光；他也无法忍受自然之声，只喜欢音乐中“经过处理的声音”。因此，这里描绘的是一个已无可挽回、奄奄一息的生态系统：这是一颗正在冷却的星球上的生命，一个被自身残骸堵塞、与任何可能的净化或更新之源隔绝的系统。如此解读，故事的核心并非灵魂的暗夜及其伴随的本体论焦虑，而是蓄意追求的生态灾难、核冬天或太阳能耗尽所带来的永恒黑暗。这是一个比传统读物通常讲述的故事更恐怖的故事，因为当叙述者从倒塌的房子里逃出来时，他将无处可逃。

The ecocentred reading, by contrast, focuses outside, on the house and its environs, rather than inside, on the owner and his psychology. It uses ideas of energy, entropy (which is a kind of negative energy within systems which tends towards breakdown and disorganisation), and symbiosis (‘sym-biosis’, literally ‘living together’, denoting mutually sustaining, co-existing systems). Thus, the house exists as an isolated entropic system which has no symbiotic connections at all with the broader biosphere. The stagnant lake reflects the house’s own unmoving image; the house breathes in the atmosphere of its own decay – the ‘gradual yet certain condensation of an atmosphere of their own about the waters and the walls.’ It has its own sealed-off microclimate, and as the climax approaches it seems to stew in its own locked-up and aborted energies, for when Usher and the narrator look out of the window ‘the exceeding density of the clouds (which hung so low as to press upon the turrets of the house) did not prevent our perceiving the lifelike velocity with which they flew careering from all points against each other, without passing away into the distance’. The House of Usher, then, is not part of a living system; no new elements come in from outside to energise it and enable it to contribute to other systems; it is a light that failed, a stream which has ceased to flow, a fire with nothing to burn. Its narcissistic aloofness from the flow of the broader life-force turns it into a kind of Black Hole, which becomes a vortex into which its energies are sucked and destroyed – ‘a whirlwind had apparently collected its force in our vicinity’ says the narrator when he looks out of the window, and we also have the black tarn (or lake) into which the house collapses and disappears at the end. Most eerie of all is Usher’s mind, ‘from which darkness, as if an inherent positive quality, poured forth upon all objects of the moral and physical universe, in one unceasing radiation of gloom’. Usher, then, radiates not energy but entropy, like an imploded star rushing towards its own disintegration. Frighteningly, he is all ‘culture’ and no ‘nature’; he is ‘photophobic’ (hyper-sensitive to light) and cannot bear natural light at all, and prefers the represented light in paintings; he cannot bear natural sounds either, only the ‘processed sound’ of music. What is imaged here, then, is an eco-system damaged beyond repair and in its death-throes: this is life on a cooling planet, a system clogged with its own detritus and cut off from any possible sources of catharsis or renewal. On this reading, the centre of the story is not a dark night of the soul, with its accompanying ontological anxieties, but the permanent night of wilfully-courted ecological disaster, nuclear winter, or solar exhaustion. This is a more frightening tale than conventional readings usually produce, for when the narrator runs from the collapsing house there will be nowhere for him to run to.

停下来思考

STOP and THINK

我所在学院系办公室的门锁在我看来是“反直觉”的——开门时，钥匙要朝向门框转动，而不是背离门框。结果就是，每次开门你都必须有意识地反其道而行之，违背直觉。批判理论为我们提供了一系列“开门钥匙”（在某些情况下，甚至是耶鲁大学的“钥匙”），其中许多似乎都基于强烈的“反直觉”基础。我的意思是，它们提出的观点似乎与我们在日常生活中本能地认为正确或真实的观念相矛盾。就生态批评而言，我们必须对抗的直觉是西方根深蒂固的、由来已久的以人为中心的文化传统，这种传统既带有宗教色彩，又体现人文主义精神，并且常常被奉为圭臬，体现在日常的格言警句中：例如，公元前五世纪的古希腊哲学家普罗泰戈拉曾说过一句名言：“人是万物的尺度”，这句名言自信地将我们置于万物的中心；在《创世记》中，人类被赋予了“管理海里的鱼、空中的鸟和一切爬行动物”的“权柄”。地面”；同样，列奥纳多·达·芬奇著名的素描《维特鲁威人》（这幅我们熟悉的图像描绘了一个裸体男性形象，置于一个圆形和一个正方形之间，双臂水平伸展，并斜举过头顶）将人体比例视为最基本几何形状的基础，因此，据说也是所有赏心悦目比例的基础；十八世纪，亚历山大·蒲柏在《人论》中写道：“认识你自己，不要妄自揣测上帝；/研究人类的恰当对象是人本身” [我的斜体]。所有这些，以及许多类似的图像和格言，似乎都赋予了我们一种高度的文化特权，让我们可以持有以人为中心而非以生态为中心的态度。

The offices in my college department have what I think of as ‘counter-intuitive’ door locks – you unlock the door by turning the key towards the door jamb, rather than away from it. The result is that you must consciously reverse the intuitively obvious procedure every time you unlock the door. Critical theory has provided us with sets of keys for unlocking doors (Yale keys, in some cases), and many of them seem to have a strongly ‘counter-intuitive’ base. By this I mean that they put forward positions which seem to contradict notions which in everyday life we tend instinctively to regard as right or true. In the case of ecocriticism, the intuition we have to counter is a long-standing, deeply-ingrained Western cultural tradition of anthropocentric attitudes, which are both religious and humanist, and often enshrined in commonplace references and sayings: thus, the early Greek philosopher Protagoras (fifth century BC) makes the famous statement ‘Man is the measure of all things’, which places us confidently at the centre of everything; in the Book of Genesis human beings are given ‘dominion’ over ‘the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that moves on the ground’; likewise, Leonardo da Vinci’s famous drawing ‘The Vitruvian Man’ (the familiar image shows a naked male figure set within a circle and a square, with arms outstretched both horizontally, and diagonally above the head) sees the proportions of the human body as the basis of the most fundamental geometrical shapes, and hence, supposedly, of all proportions which please the eye; and in the eighteenth century Alexander Pope writes (in An Essay on Man) ‘Know then thyself, presume not God to scan; / The proper study of mankind is Man’ [my italics]. All these, and many more images and sayings like them, seem to give us a high cultural licence for attitudes which are anthropocentric rather than ecocentric.

十九世纪，伟大的维多利亚时代艺术评论家约翰·罗斯金在其著作《现代画家》第三卷（1856年）中创造了“拟人谬误”一词，用来描述我们本能地倾向于将自身情感投射到周围环境中的倾向。这似乎是另一种形式的习惯，即认为一切都以我们自身为中心。他写道：“所有强烈的情感都会产生相同的效果。它们使我们对外部事物的所有印象都产生虚假性，我通常将其称为‘拟人谬误’。”因此，像“残酷的大海”这样的短语就体现了拟人谬误，因为它将人类的属性（残酷）投射到自然元素上。罗斯金是一位具有深刻环保意识的英国重要作家，他是第一位记录下自然恢复能力可能并非无限，以及现代生产和消费方式有可能对环境造成致命破坏的英国作家。在他关于他称之为“十九世纪的风暴云”（他也称之为“现代的瘟疫云”）的演讲中，他表达了对大气正因工业污染而遭受永久性破坏的深切担忧。我们可以说，这正是我们自以为对自然的“支配”没有限制所导致的后果。经过二十年的观察，这位“富有远见”的罗斯金确信，在此期间，云的形成、大气状况和天气模式都发生了变化。

In the nineteenth century the great Victorian art critic John Ruskin, in his Modern Painters, vol. 3 (1856), coined the term the ‘pathetic fallacy’ for our instinctive tendency to see our emotions reflected in our environment, which seems to be another form of the habit of seeing everything as centred upon ourselves: ‘All violent feelings’, he says, ‘have the same effect. They produce in us a falseness in all our impressions of external things, which I would generally characterize as the “pathetic fallacy”’. Hence, a phrase like ‘the cruel sea’ manifests the pathetic fallacy by projecting a human attribute (cruelty) onto a natural element. Ruskin was deeply eco-conscious, the first major British writer to record a sense that nature’s powers of recovery might not be infinite, and that modern forms of production and consumption have the potential to inflict fatal environmental damage: in his lectures on what he called ‘the storm-cloud of the nineteenth century’, which he also called ‘the modern plague-cloud’, he expressed his deep anxiety that the atmosphere was being permanently damaged by industrial pollution, which we might say was the environmental consequence of assuming that our ‘dominion’ over nature need have no limits. The ‘minatory’ Ruskin is convinced, after twenty years of making observations, that cloud formations, atmospheric conditions, and weather patterns had changed (had been changed) during that time.

有趣的是，相比之下，爱默生却丝毫不担心移情谬误——“自然总是披着精神的色彩”。他在《自然》第一章中写道，很难不认同他的观点。如果说这两位人物在这个问题上的分歧，正是前文提到的美英生态批评分歧的体现，这种说法是否过于牵强？将这两种观点分别贴上环境乐观主义和环境悲观主义的标签，是否过于简单化？像英国和日本这样人口稠密的岛屿，是否更容易让人产生一种直觉，觉得自然正在被文化迅速吞噬？而像美国或澳大利亚这样幅员辽阔的陆地，是否仅仅因为其周边环境的存在，就更容易让人从心底里相信地球终将幸存，无论全球变暖和臭氧层破坏的证据如何？无论我们本能地倾向于哪一种观点，我们自身对问题的善意认知真的能起到作用吗？世界秩序需要发生哪些改变才能改善现状？而这些改变是否必然会限制我们的自由？毕竟，是什么让罗斯金有自由去写作和担忧工业污染（而其他人却不得不为了生计而辛勤劳作）？归根结底，难​​道不是建立在雪利酒进口基础上的家族财富吗？而雪利酒进口这种贸易，必然与其他任何贸易一样，与造成工业污染的因素有着千丝万缕的联系。我们自身的生活，我们阅读的书籍、学习的课程、浏览的网站，难道就与工业污染无关吗？

Interestingly, Emerson, by contrast, had no worries about the pathetic fallacy – ‘Nature always wears the colours of the spirit’, he says, in the first chapter of Nature, and it is difficult not to sympathise with what he is saying. Is it going too far to suggest that the difference between these two figures on this point is symptomatic of that divergent tendency between US and UK ecocriticism mentioned earlier? Is it an over-simplification to label the two viewpoints as symptomatic of (respectively) environmental optimism and environmental pessimism? Are crowded islands like Britain and Japan likely to inspire the gut feeling that nature is rapidly being gobbled up by culture, while on the other hand, vast land-masses like America or Australia tend by their very surrounding presence, to produce the deep-down conviction that the earth will survive, no matter what evidence there might be about global warming and the ozone layer? Whichever way we instinctively incline on this, can our own well-meant awareness of the problem make any difference? What changes in the world order will be needed to make an improvement in the situation, and will they inevitably curtail our freedoms? After all, what gave Ruskin the freedom to write about and worry about industrial pollution (while other men and women had to sweat for a living)? Wasn’t it, ultimately, the family fortune, which was based on the importing of sherry, a trade which must be as intimately linked as any other to the forces which produce industrial pollution? Can our own lives, of books, and courses, and web-sites, be any less implicated?

生态批评家做什么

What ecocritics do

1. 他们从生态中心主义的角度重新阅读了重要的文学作品，特别关注对自然世界的描写。

1. They re-read major literary works from an ecocentric perspective, with particular attention to the representation of the natural world.

2. 它们扩展了一系列生态中心概念的适用范围，将这些概念应用于自然界以外的事物——例如增长和能量、平衡和失衡、共生和互惠以及能源和资源的可持续或不可持续利用等概念。

2. They extend the applicability of a range of ecocentric concepts, using them of things other than the natural world – concepts such as growth and energy, balance and imbalance, symbiosis and mutuality, and sustainable or unsustainable uses of energy and resources.

3. 他们特别重视那些将自然作为其主题主要部分的作家，例如……美国超验主义者、英国浪漫主义者、约翰·克莱尔的诗歌、托马斯·哈代的作品以及二十世纪初乔治王朝时期的诗人。

3. They give special canonical emphasis to writers who foreground nature as a major part of their subject matter, such as the American transcendentalists, the British Romantics, the poetry of John Clare, the work of Thomas Hardy and the Georgian poets of the early twentieth century.

4. 他们通过强调相关的“事实性”写作，特别是反思性的地形材料，如散文、游记、回忆录和地方文学，扩展了文学批评实践的范围。

4. They extend the range of literary-critical practice by placing a new emphasis on relevant ‘factual’ writing, especially reflective topographical material such as essays, travel writing, memoirs, and regional literature.

5. 他们摒弃了主流文学理论的“社会建构主义”和“语言决定论”（强调外部世界的语言和社会建构性），转而强调以生态为中心的价值观，即细致的观察、集体的道德责任以及我们自身之外的世界的诉求。

5. They turn away from the ‘social constructivism’ and ‘linguistic determinism’ of dominant literary theories (with their emphasis on the linguistic and social constructedness of the external world) and instead emphasise ecocentric values of meticulous observation, collective ethical responsibility, and the claims of the world beyond ourselves.

生态批评：一个例子

Ecocriticism: an example

1915年，年迈的托马斯·哈代，随着第一次世界大战的持续，深感文明价值观的崩溃，于是写了一首短诗，名为《在“国家分裂”之时》：

In 1915 the aging Thomas Hardy, overwhelmed by a sense of the collapse of civilised values as the Great War dragged on, wrote a brief poem called ‘In Time of “The Breaking of Nations”’:

我

只是一个人，拖着沉重的泥土，

缓慢而无声地走着，

和一匹老马，它踉跄着，点头晃脑，

半睡半醒地跟在后面。

I

Only a man harrowing clods

In a slow silent walk

With an old horse that stumbles and nods

Half asleep as they stalk.

二、

只有稀薄的烟雾，没有火焰，

从成堆的狗牙根草中升起；然而，即使王朝更迭，

这景象仍将如常。

II

Only thin smoke without flame

From the heaps of couch-grass;

Yet this will go onward the same

Though Dynasties pass.

三、

远处，一位少女和她的亡灵

低语而来：

战争的编年史将在夜幕

降临之前，被黑暗笼罩。

III

Yonder a maid and her wight

Come whispering by:

War’s annals will cloud into night

Ere their story die.

随着“王朝更迭”，国家在战火中分崩离析，诗人绝望地环顾四周，寻找永恒不变的例证。他试图让自己确信，尽管经历了世界大战的灾难，仍然有一些永恒不变的事物会永远“一成不变地”存在；而他选择的事物是低技术农业实践中最常见的表现形式——一个耕夫用马拉犁耕地，“一个男人在缓慢而安静的行走中耙土”。

As ‘Dynasties pass’ and nations are broken in the onslaught, the poet desperately looks round him for an example of immutability, seeking to re-assure himself that there is something permanent which will ‘go onward the same’ for ever, in spite of the catastrophe of world war; and the something he chooses is that most commonplace manifestation of low-tech agricultural practice – a ploughman working a field with a horse-drawn plough, ‘a man harrowing clods / In a slow silent walk’.

但说这首诗写于1915年只是字面上的说法；更准确的说法是，它是在1915年被记录下来的，因为诗中提到的那位农夫实际上在1870年就被哈代在康沃尔郡一位牧师住宅的花园里见过，当时他正在追求他的第一任妻子艾玛·拉维尼亚·吉福德。从更广阔的生态学角度来看，我们可以说，在他如今已遥远的个人过往中，一个想法的种子在他心中种下，一个意象随着时间的推移而生长成熟，最终被重新利用，以满足多年后出现的需求。因此，这首诗的孕育过程本身就反映了诗中所描绘的耐心成长和培育的过程。正如哈代在其第二任妻子代笔的自传中所述，他与艾玛的恋情发生在早前的一场欧洲冲突——1870-1871年的普法战争期间。1915年诗歌中出现的农夫形象，正是1870年8月18日——“格拉沃洛特血战”（普鲁士取得胜利，但普鲁士方面伤亡2万人，法国方面伤亡1.3万人）当天所见。当时，哈代和艾玛正在户外一起阅读丁尼生的诗歌。尽管在此期间一切都发生了变化或消逝——旧欧洲秩序的瓦解、他小说中记录的农业耕作方式的变革、他自己的青春岁月的逝去、两人之间多年疏离的痛苦，以及最终艾玛的离世——哈代仍然相信永恒不变，相信自然的力量是永恒的、取之不尽的。因此，这位“永恒”的农夫在哈代的脑海中停留了四十五年而未曾改变，体现了哈代所追求的超越时间的特质。相比之下，“少女和她的侍从”并非哈代在1870年或1915年所见的真人，而是他和爱玛在1870年场景中的一种回溯性的“投射”，他们因与这位永恒的农夫的关联而被卷入永恒的虚构之中——这位不可知论诗人将农夫塑造成未来以及自然和人类不朽的某种保证。

But it’s only literally true to say that the poem was written in 1915; it would be more accurate to say that it was written down in 1915, since the remembered ploughman had actually been seen by Hardy in 1870, from the garden of a rectory in Cornwall when he was courting his first wife, Emma Lavinia Gifford. Thinking of this from a broadly ecological perspective, we might say that in his now remote personal past, the seed of an idea was planted in the poet’s mind, an image grew and matured over time, and was eventually re-cycled to meet a need which arose many years later. So the gestation of the poem itself mirrors the patient processes of growth and cultivation which are depicted in it. As Hardy relates in the autobiography ‘ghosted’ by his second wife, the courtship with Emma took place during an earlier European conflict, the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–1871, and the ploughman used in the 1915 poem was seen on 18 August 1870, the day of ‘the bloody battle of Gravelotte’ (a Prussian victory that cost 20,000 Prussian casualties and 13,000 French), when Hardy and Emma had been reading Tennyson together outdoors. In spite of all that had changed or passed away in the meantime – the old European order, the transformations in farming practices which his own novels had recorded, the passing of his own youth, the years of estranged bitterness between the two of them, and finally the death of Emma herself – Hardy still believed in durance and immutability, in natural forces which are timeless and inexhaustible. The ‘timeless’ ploughman, therefore, lives on for forty-five years in his mind without alteration, embodying the time-defying qualities Hardy seeks. The ‘maid and her wight’, by contrast, are not persons seen by Hardy, either in 1870 or in 1915, but a retrospective ‘back projection’ of himself and Emma into that 1870 scene, drawn into the artifice of eternity by their association with the ever-enduring ploughman, the figure whom the agnostic poet makes into a kind of guarantee of the future and of the indestructibility of nature and humanity.

就前文所述的景观图景而言，诗中悠闲的叙述者/观察者徘徊于第三和第四区域之间，从牧师住宅的花园向外眺望（花园是种植观赏性植物以求审美和感官愉悦的地方，因此也是传统的休闲和情爱场所——“来花园吧，莫德！”）。他眺望着耕地山谷，即第三区域，这里是种植作物以维持生计的地方，也是人们辛勤劳作以实现美好生活的场所。农业和园艺这两个区域彼此相邻，哈代通过将求爱的男女投射到“彼岸”，也就是花园之外，暗示了二者之间的理想融合，并赋予他们共同的特质——马和人缓慢、沉默、半梦半醒，少女和白马低语，因此也行动缓慢。整个场景缓慢而静谧地进行着，仿佛处于催眠状态，但它们并未完全融为一体。第一节中的农夫和第三节中的夫妇被第二节中更为负面的意象所分隔——燃烧的草堆中升起稀薄的烟雾，却不见火焰，仿佛原本和谐共生的景象，在地方和家庭的田园风光中，被一种不祥的预兆所打破。所有那些徘徊在诗歌之外的破坏性人类活动（标题引自耶利米书的经文中所指的国家分裂，以及自传中提到的普法战争）撕裂并错位了这两个区域，并以燃烧的景象为象征。我们可以说，这两个区域之间，或者说生命中这些不同阶段和层面之间的共生关系，正受到战争带来的熵增式屠戮的威胁。

In terms of the landscape schema given earlier, the leisured speaker/observer in the poem is poised between areas three and four, looking out from the rectory garden (gardens being the place of decorative flora intended for aesthetic and sensuous pleasure, and hence a traditional setting for relaxation and erotic dalliance – ‘Come into the garden, Maud’!). He looks out into the valley of arable land, area three, locus of planting for sustenance, and scene of the labour required to bring the good life to fruition. The two regions, agriculture and horticulture, adjoin each other and Hardy implies an ideal fusion between them by projecting the courting couple out ‘yonder’, which is to say beyond the garden, giving them attributes in common – horse and man slow and silent and half asleep, maid and wight whispering and hence also moving slowly. The whole scene moves slowly and quietly, as if under hypnosis, but they are not quite fused into one, for the ploughman in the first stanza and the couple in the third are divided by the second stanza, with its more negative image – thin smoke without flame from the heaps of burning grass, as if the vision of united, productive harmony across the local and domestic landscape is ominously interrupted. All that destructive human activity which hovers just beyond the poem (the breaking of nations referred to in the title’s quotation from Jeremiah, and the battles of the Franco-Prussian war mentioned in the autobiography) splits and dislocates the two areas, and is represented by the burning. The symbiosis between the two areas, we might say, between these different phases and aspects of life, is threatened by the entropic carnage of war.

饱受战争带来的破坏和浪费之苦，我们不禁要问，这对夫妇又能从丁尼生的诗歌中找到什么慰藉呢？他们读的是丁尼生的哪首诗呢？是那首爱国主义的、如同纸上谈兵的《轻骑兵的冲锋》（据他儿子说，他儿子读到《泰晤士报》对这场冲锋的报道时激动不已，在房间里挥舞着报纸，像挥舞一把假军刀一样）吗？还是那首歌颂科技变革和铁路兴起、几乎不带任何环境焦虑的《洛克斯利庄园》？又或是那首忧郁的《悼念集》？那首诗的作者似乎对生命永无止境抱有怀疑，因为他意识到物种灭绝的化石记录（当时人们正在逐渐解读这些记录）终将消亡。这些由维多利亚时代早期地质学家（其中许多是业余牧师）撰写的著作，并没有传递出一种令人安心的、自然界良性延续的信息，而是生动地描绘了一种生命力，这种生命力甚至对无数物种的消失都毫不在意，描绘了一个“弱肉强食、弱不禁风”的自然，其驱动力并非出于爱，而是出于无情的掠夺本能。丁尼生以他的不可知论视角（这与哈代相似——他“信奉教会”，但并非虔诚的信徒）来描述山峦和大陆，它们的形态和特征毫无持久性可言，（从地质年代的角度来看）如同云朵般变幻莫测。因此，在丁尼生的诗歌中寻找慰藉的话语可能相当困难，所以诗人转而在周围的世界中寻求慰藉，而不是在阅读中寻求慰藉，于是他想到了农夫的形象。

Burdened with a sense of the disruptive waste of war, what comfort, we might ask, could the couple have found in Tennyson? What Tennyson poems might they have been reading? Was it the work of the patriotic, armchair-warrior Tennyson of ‘The Charge of the Light Brigade’ (according to his son, so excited by the Times account of that charge that he whooped about the room swishing the newspaper round above his head like a mock sabre)? Or the Tennyson of ‘Locksley Hall’, who celebrated technological change and the coming of the railways, with little sign of any environmental anxieties? Or the sombre Tennyson of ‘In Memoriam’, who seemed to have little trust in life going on forever, for he realised that the fossil record of the loss and extinction of species (then gradually being interpreted by pioneer Victorian geologists, many of whom were clergymen amateurs) carried no re-assuring message of a benign, natural continuity, but told vividly of a life force that cared nothing even for the disappearance of innumerable entire species, and of ‘nature red in tooth and claw’, driven by ruthless predatory instincts rather than by love? This Tennyson spoke from his agnosticism (which was similar to Hardy’s – he was ‘churchy’, but not solidly religious) of hills and continents whose forms and identities are quite without durance and (when viewed across the vista of geological aeons) seem as fluid as cloud formations.8 Finding words of comfort in Tennyson, then, would probably have been pretty difficult, so that the poet looks for comfort in the world around him, rather than in his reading, and so lights upon the figure of the ploughman.

从我们当下的视角来看，沉思于农夫这一“永恒”形象所重拾的信心，似乎有些过于乐观，甚至自欺欺人——哈代笔下永恒不变的形象，在我们看来，恰恰是脆弱的象征，它让人联想起一个逝去的、以人为本的农业时代，一个遥远的过去，那时人们对农业的主要印象并非是政府补贴的过度生产、疯牛病和口蹄疫等疾病，以及鸣禽和篱笆的消失。如此解读，便开启了一种以生态为中心的诗歌解读，这种解读并非聚焦于作者个人生活的悲情，而是聚焦于两者之间奇特的对比：一方面，诗人仿佛拥有无限的时间，用毕生心血孕育一个诗歌意象；另一方面，生态平衡的脆弱性也清晰可见，而这正是农夫这一形象所必须向我们揭示的。

From the perspective of our own present, the confidence which is restored by contemplating the ‘timeless’ figure of the ploughman will seem somewhat over-optimistic and self-deluding – Hardy’s figure of immutability would be our emblem of fragility, a being redolent of a vanished era of human-scale agriculture and of a remote time when the primary associations of farming were not with subsidised over-production, diseases like BSE and Foot and Mouth, and the disappearance of song-birds and hedge-rows. To react in this way is to begin to frame an ecocentred reading of the poem, centred, that is, not on the pathos of the author’s personal life, but on that bizarre contrast between, on the one hand, the loving incubation of a single poetic image across a whole lifetime, as if a poet had all the time in the world, and, on the other, the actual precariousness of the ecological balance, which is what that figure must embody for us.

总之，这种以生态为中心的阅读方式有哪些特征？以下列表旨在说明我这种带有生态色彩的阅读方式的尝试，而非其最终成果，但我希望它能体现生态批评阅读的常见特征。首先，评论中体现了广义生态思想的融入，具体表现为：例如，我们需要敏锐地意识到诗歌本身的成长过程，它并非凭空产生，而是在诗人一生中层层叠加而成，并非灵感迸发、缺乏明显支撑的瞬间产物。其次，读者会意识到，构成诗歌缓慢成长的素材丰富多样，既有真实发生的事件——有些来自过去，有些来自现在——也有想象的投射，因此，这首诗并非简单意义上的“真实”，而是具有更为强大的“贴近生活”的特质。第三，当然，诗歌中也明确地包含了生态层面的内容（再次提及环境“区域”的素材），这些内容在讨论中也占据了应有的分量。第四，我们从诗歌中解读出一种尖锐的、回顾性的反讽（即，在哈代创作这首诗不到一个世纪之后，它所象征的永恒在我们这里已不再适用），这种反讽源于我们自身对环境危机和危险的深刻感知。最后（也是所有这些的总和），这种解读本身是多元且兼收并蓄的，它不拘泥于单一议题（例如寓言式的平行关系或某种深奥的象征意义），而是具有方法论上的平衡和开放性，使其能够从广泛的材料中汲取养分，而不是像大多数批评方法那样局限于单一类型的证据（例如，形式主义批评家纯粹依赖文本，马克思主义批评家主要依赖历史，解构主义者主要依赖反直觉的语言元素，等等）。这种兼收并蓄的特点在生态批评的解读中往往非常显著，但通常不被提及，因为对批评方法的焦虑似乎与这种方法有些遥远。美国生态批评家斯科特·斯洛维克的一句名言恰好概括了这种态度；斯洛维克引用了沃尔特·惠特曼在《自我之歌》中的一句诗，诗中诗人宣称“我博大精深，包罗万象”，并将其应用于生态批评群体，补充道：“没有单一的、主导性的世界观指导生态批评实践——在生态批评的写作或教学中，没有单一的策略在起作用”（库普，160）。当然，大多数批评和理论运动都对自身做出类似的兼收并蓄的宣称，即使是那些与某位创始人物的洞见紧密相关的运动（例如弗洛伊德、拉康、福柯、德里达等），但引人注目的是，在生态批评领域，并没有任何一位人物拥有这种主导地位——生态批评本身就是一个多元化的生态系统。

What, in conclusion, are some of the characteristics of this kind of ecocentric reading? The list below indicates what my ecologically inflected reading attempted, rather than what it perhaps achieved, but it is illustrative, I hope, of the traits which ecocritical readings commonly have. So, firstly, the commentary gives evidence of the incorporation of broadly conceived ecological thinking, showing, for instance, a keen awareness of the growth processes of the poem itself, how it builds in several layers across a lifetime, and does not come into being in a single flash of inspired imaginative insight which has no visible means of support. Secondly, the reading is aware that the materials which contribute to the poem’s slow growth are diverse and disparate, some are actual events – some from the past some from the present – and others are imaginative projections, so that the poem isn’t ‘true’ in any simplistic way, but has the much more potent quality of ‘truth-to-life’. Thirdly, of course, an explicitly ecological level of content has been identified (the material about the ‘areas’ of environment again), and these too have appropriate weight in the discussion. Fourthly, we have read back into the poem a hard-edged, retrospective irony (that its emblem of permanence cannot function as that for us, less than a century after Hardy wrote the poem), this irony arising from our own acute sense of environmental crisis and danger. Finally (which is the sum of these), the reading is itself diverse and eclectic, not hidebound by a single issue (such as an allegorical parallel or some kind of esoteric symbolism) but having a methodological balance and openness which allows it to build from a wide range of materials, not restricting itself, in the way that most critical approaches do, to a single type of evidence (purely textual for the ‘Formalist’ critic, predominantly historical for the Marxist, mainly counter-intuitive linguistic elements for the deconstructor, and so on). Such eclecticism is often very marked in ecocritical readings, but not usually remarked upon, since anxieties about critical method can seem somewhat remote from this approach. A well-known remark by American ecocritic Scott Slovic comes to mind as encapsulating this attitude; Slovic quotes Walt Whitman’s line in ‘Song of Myself’ in which the speaker proclaims ‘I am large, I contain multitudes’ and applies it to the community of ecocritics, adding ‘There is no single, dominant world-view guiding ecocritical practice – no single strategy at work from example to example of ecocritical writing or teaching’ (Coupe, 160). Of course, most critical and theoretical movements make the same eclectic claim about themselves, even those which are closely aligned with the insights of a single founding figure (such as Freud, Lacan, Foucault, Derrida, etc.), but it is striking that there is no single figure within ecocriticism who has that kind of dominance – ecocriticism itself is a diverse biosphere.

精选读物

Selected reading

读者

Readers

Branch, Michael P. 和 Slovic, Scott 编，《ISLE 读者：生态批评：1993-2003》（佐治亚大学出版社，2003 年）。

与 Coupe、Glotfelty 和 Kerridge/Sammells 竞争的“官方”竞争对手。

Branch, Michael P. and Slovic, Scott, eds, The ISLE Reader: Ecocriticism: 1993-2003 (University of Georgia Press, 2003).

An ‘official’ rival to Coupe, Glotfelty, and Kerridge/Sammells.

劳伦斯·库普主编，《绿色研究读本：从浪漫主义到生态批评》（劳特利奇出版社，2000年）。

这是英国最权威的绿色研究文集，不仅收录了英国当代重要学者（如索珀、斯奈德、斯洛维克、布埃尔、罗扎克、格洛特费尔蒂等）的观点，也涵盖了浪漫主义时期以来的早期作品。全书共五十章，篇幅短小，分为六个精心构思且导言详实的章节，因此全书篇幅控制在300页左右。

Coupe, Laurence, ed. The Green Studies Reader: From Romanticism to Ecocriticism (Routledge, 2000).

This is the definitive UK collection, but it represents major contemporary American voices (Soper, Snyder, Slovic, Buell, Roszak, Glotfelty, etc.) as well as British ones (Bate, Gifford, Garrard, Kerridge, etc.), and includes earlier material from the Romantic period onwards. Fifty chapters, mostly quite short, in six well conceived and well introduced sections, so the book is kept to a sensible size of around 300 pages.

Glotfelty, Cheryll 和 Fromm, Harold 编，《生态批评读本：文学生态学的里程碑》（佐治亚大学出版社，1996 年）。

上述书籍的美国竞争对手——另一部优秀的文集，但篇幅并不庞大（简洁明了是生态批评的美德）。

Glotfelty, Cheryll and Fromm, Harold, eds, The Ecocriticism Reader: Landmarks in Literary Ecology (University of Georgia Press, 1996).

The US rival of the above – another excellent, but not mammoth, collection (brevity and concision are ecocritical virtues).

克里奇、理查德和萨梅尔斯、尼尔编，《环境写作》（Zed Books出版社，1998年）。

本书收录了十五篇由英国和美国该领域主要学者撰写的文章，分为三个部分——“生态批评理论”、“生态批评史”和“当代写作”。尽管库普的文集后来也出版了，但本书仍然是一本实用且引人入胜的著作。

Kerridge, Richard and Sammells, Neil, eds, Writing the Environment (Zed Books, 1998).

Fifteen essays by major British and American contributors to the field, in three sections – ‘Ecocritical theory’, ‘Ecocritical history’, and ‘Contemporary writing’. Still a useful and engaging book, in spite of the subsequent publication of Coupe’s collection.

一般的

General

乔纳森·贝特，《浪漫生态学：华兹华斯与环境传统》（劳特利奇出版社，1991年）。

本书已成为经典之作，是当代英国生态批评的奠基之作，篇幅精简，引人深思，引人入胜。

Bate, Jonathan, Romantic Ecology: Wordsworth and the Environmental Tradition (Routledge, 1991).

Already a classic; the founding text of contemporary British ecocriticism: a brief, thought-provoking and engaging book.

乔纳森·贝特，《大地之歌》（Picador出版社，2000年）。

本书视野开阔，选段丰富多样，令人印象深刻。它展现了这种方法能够充分利用技巧、学识和热情。

Bate, Jonathan, The Song of the Earth (Picador, 2000).

Impressive for its overall scope and for the breadth and variety of the individual readings. The book shows that this approach can make full use of technique and learning as well as zeal.

劳伦斯·布埃尔，《环境想象：梭罗、自然写作与美国文化的形成》（哈佛大学出版社，1995年）。

这是一部在该领域极具意义和影响力的著作——也是生态批评家引用最多的书籍。

Buell, Lawrence, The Environmental Imagination: Thoreau, Nature Writing, and the Formation of American Culture (Harvard University Press, 1995).

A highly significant and influential work in this field – this is the book most frequently cited by ecocritics.

伊根，加布里埃尔，《绿色莎士比亚：从生态政治到生态批评》（劳特利奇出版社，“莎士比亚研究”系列，2006 年）。

论生态批评的“增长领域”——一本充满活力、出自创新系列的著作。

Egan, Gabriel, Green Shakespeare: From Ecopolitics to Ecocriticism (Routledge, ‘Accents on Shakespeare’ series, 2006).

On a ‘growth area’ in ecocriticism – a lively book in an innovative series.

Garrard, Greg，《生态批评》（Routledge，“新批评语汇”系列，2004 年）。

这是一本非常实用且简洁的生态批评领域指南。

Garrard, Greg, Ecocriticism (Routledge, ‘New Critical Idiom’ series, 2004).

A very useful and succinct guide to the field.

吉福德，特里，《绿色之声：理解当代自然诗歌》（曼彻斯特大学出版社，1995 年）。

书中讨论了 R.S. 托马斯、乔治·麦凯·布朗、约翰·蒙塔古、诺曼·尼科尔森、帕特里克·卡瓦纳等人，他称之为克拉布和克莱尔的“反田园诗”传统；以及，在他所谓的“后田园诗”模式中，希尼（华兹华斯的继承者）和休斯（布莱克的继承者）。

Gifford, Terry, Green Voices: Understanding Contemporary Nature Poetry (Manchester University Press, 1995).

Discusses R. S. Thomas, George Mackay Brown, John Montague, Norman Nicholson, Patrick Kavanagh, and others in what he calls the ‘anti-pastoralist’ tradition of Crabbe and Clare; and, in what he calls the ‘post-pastoral’ mode, Heaney (successor to Wordsworth) and Hughes (successor to Blake).

吉福德，特里，《牧区》（劳特利奇出版社，“批判习语”系列，1999 年）。

这是一本非常有用的书，它发展了前一本书中使用的牧区、反牧区和后牧区的三层模型。

Gifford, Terry, Pastoral (Routledge, ‘Critical Idiom’ series, 1999).

A very useful book developing the three-layer model of pastoral, anti-pastoral, and post-pastoral used in the previous book.

克罗伯，卡尔，《生态文学批评：浪漫主义想象与心灵生物学》（哥伦比亚大学出版社，1994 年）。

这是一本篇幅短小、引人入胜的书，非常适合与贝茨的两部著作（见上文）搭配阅读。

Kroeber, Karl, Ecological Literary Criticism: Romantic Imagining and the Biology of Mind (Columbia University Press, 1994).

Another brief and engaging book, making an ideal paired read with either of Bate’s (above).

墨菲，帕特里克·D.（编）。《自然文学：国际资料汇编》（菲茨罗伊·迪尔伯恩出版社，1998年）。

“这是一部参考著作，探讨了自然以及人类与自然界其他部分互动的文学表现形式的多样性、模式和取向。”

Murphy, Patrick D., ed. Literature of Nature: An International Source-book (Fitzroy Dearborn, 1998).

‘A reference work that explores the diversity of genres, modes, and orientations of literary representations of nature and of human interaction with the rest of the natural world.’

普拉姆伍德，瓦尔，《女权主义与自然的掌控》（劳特利奇出版社，1993年）。

“探讨了生态女权主义或生态女性主义的兴起，解释了它与其他女权主义理论以及诸如深层生态学等激进绿色理论的关系。”

Plumwood, Val, Feminism and the Mastery of Nature (Routledge, 1993).

‘Explores the emergence of ecofeminism or ecological feminism, explaining its relation to other feminist theories, and to radical green theories such as deep ecology.’

西蒙·沙玛，《风景与记忆》（哈珀·柯林斯出版社，1995年）。

“环境如何影响历史？……本书试图回答这些问题，并描绘我们周围的世界以及它如何塑造我们。”

Schama, Simon, Landscape and Memory (Harper Collins, 1995).

‘How does environment influence history? … This work attempts to answer these questions and gives a portrait of the world around us and how it shapes us.’

索珀，凯特，《什么是自然？文化、政治与非人类》（布莱克威尔出版社，1995 年）。

这是 20 世纪 90 年代中期另一部可读性强且意义深远的著作，奠定了当代生态批评的基础。

Soper, Kate, What is Nature? Culture, Politics, and the Non-Human (Blackwell, 1995).

Another readable and fundamental text from the mid 1990s period which laid the foundations of contemporary ecocriticism.

14文学理论——十个事件的

历史

14

Literary theory – a history

in ten events

市面上一些文学理论入门指南都包含关键术语表、“时间轴”以及以百科全书形式编排的重要理论家思想简介等内容。我并没有打算在本书第三版中加入这些内容，因为我始终倾向于将信息整合到一个主题叙事中。然而，讲述文学理论发展历程的一种方法是，围绕构成其公共历史的一系列关键事件展开。这样做的好处在于，许多潜在主题得以凸显，从而使理论的轨迹——其兴衰的弧线——清晰地展现出来。当然，我在这里使用“文学理论”一词时，指的是其从二十世纪中期开始的复兴，而忽略了第一章中提及的早期理论史。在这些限制条件下，我们可以通过十个关键事件来讲述理论的故事。

Several of the available introductory guides to literary theory incorporate such features as glossaries of key terms, ‘timelines’, and potted accounts of the ideas of important theorists arranged in encyclopaedic format. I have not been tempted to include any of these features in the third edition of this book, because I have always preferred to integrate information into a themed narrative. But one way of presenting the story of literary theory is to centre it upon a series of the key events which constitute its public history. The advantage of doing this is that many of the underlying themes are thereby brought to the fore, so that the trajectory of theory – the arc of its rise and fall – becomes strikingly apparent. Of course, I am using the term ‘literary theory’ here in its narrow sense, which is to say in reference to its resurgence from the mid twentieth century onwards, and disregarding the earlier history of theory which was touched upon in Chapter 1. Within these limitations, we can tell the story of theory through ten key events.

1958年印第安纳大学“风格研讨会”

The Indiana University ‘Conference on Style’, 1958

阅读：有关会议论文集，请参阅Thomas A. Sebeok 编辑的《语言风格》，麻省理工学院出版社，1960 年。

Reading: for the book of the conference see Style in Language, ed. Thomas A. Sebeok, The M.I.T. Press, 1960.

在其早期阶段（如第二章所述），文学理论直接源于语言学的发展。1958年在印第安纳州举行的跨学科“风格研讨会”可以被视为语言学在文学理论中日益重要的标志。人文科学。托马斯·塞贝克（1920-2001）是本次会议的召集人，他是一位匈牙利语言学学者，于1944年入籍美国。他早期的博士研究导师是语言学家罗曼·雅各布森，雅各布森的“闭幕词：（语言学与诗学）”成为本次会议最具影响力的成果。但本次会议最具创新性的特点在于其跨学科性：它从语言学、文学批评和心理学这三个相关学科的角度探讨了风格问题（如何定义风格、如何描述风格、如何研究风格的影响）。然而，论文的整体倾向明显偏向语言学。会议论文集分为九个部分，其中四个部分分别聚焦于音系学、韵律学、语法学和语义学，这些都是语言学的主要研究领域；第五部分题为“语言学视角下的语言艺术”，第六部分则仅仅是开篇和结尾的陈述（分别来自三个参与学科）。由此可见，语言学的影响力正显著扩展到其他两个领域——尤其是文学批评领域——并步入其主导地位和声望的鼎盛时期。因此，本次会议标志着人文学科内部权力平衡的显著转变，标志着科学研究方法的影响力不断扩大，并逐渐成为公认的研究模式，从自然科学扩展到社会科学，如今又延伸至人文学科。事实上，这本收录了会议论文的会议记录册中充满了图表和统计分析表格：如果你不经意间从书架上取下它，翻阅之后可能会误以为它是一部科学专著。作者们旨在论证事实的真伪，而非仅仅试图说服我们他们的断言是正确的。他们想要证明某些断言是正确的，而不仅仅是论证它们是正确的，而这正是科学方法的精髓所在。

In its early phase (as explained in Chapter 2), literary theory was the direct offspring of developments in linguistics. The interdisciplinary ‘Conference on Style’ at Indiana in 1958 can be seen as an important marker of the growing importance of linguistics within the Humanities. Thomas Sebeok (1920–2001), who convened the conference, was a Hungarian scholar in linguistics who had become an American citizen in 1944. His doctoral studies at the outset of his career had been supervised by the linguist Roman Jakobson, whose ‘Closing Statement: (Linguistics and Poetics)’ became the most lastingly influential item of the conference. But the most innovative feature of the conference itself was its interdisciplinarity: it debated the question of style (how to define it, how to describe it, how to investigate its effects) from the viewpoints of three relevant disciplines, these being linguistics, literary criticism, and psychology. However, the overall bias of the papers was very much dominated by linguistics, and of the nine sections into which the book of the conference is divided, four of them centre on phonology, metrics, grammar, and semantics, respectively, which are prime areas of investigation in linguistics, while the fifth is called ‘Linguistic approaches to verbal art’, and the sixth is merely the collection of opening and closing statements (one of each from the three contributing disciplines). So there is a strong sense of linguistics extending its influence into the other two spheres – but especially into literary criticism – and entering the era of its highest dominance and prestige. Hence, the conference signals a distinct shift in the balance of power within the Humanities, marking the moment when the scientific method of enquiry extends its empire, and becomes the accepted model of enquiry in general, spreading from the sciences, to the social sciences, and now into the Humanities. Indeed, the book of the conference, which reproduces papers delivered at the event, abounds with diagrams, graphs, and tables of statistical analysis: if you had taken it down from the shelf without realising what it was, you might assume on flicking through that it is a scientific treatise of some kind. Its writers aim to demonstrate what is or is not the case, rather than seeking merely to persuade us that what they assert is truly the case. They want to prove that certain assertions are true, rather than merely arguing that they are, and that is the essence of the scientific method.

当然，这次会议并没有解决这些问题，而且实际上有三份闭幕陈述，并非只有雅各布森的，正如人们通常认为的那样。代表文学批评的闭幕陈述是：著名批评家勒内·韦勒克对此深表怀疑。尽管如此，新批评派人文主义方法在文学研究领域的主导地位正走向尾声，语言学的声望也日益提升——美国语言学家诺姆·乔姆斯基生于1922年，即将成为他那一代语言学思想界的领军人物，其影响力堪比半个世纪前的索绪尔。乔姆斯基的第一本书《句法结构》（ 1957）已经出版，一些与会者在会议上也讨论了这本书。运用语言学概念很快将成为理论研究的默认方式，部分原因在于乔姆斯基的著作取得了巨大成功，他论证了语法和语义（即意义）不可分割，并且“深层”句法结构才是意义的最终决定因素。*雅各布森的总结陈词并未试图概括会议期间提出的论点。相反，他对诗歌的深入技术性分析展现了语言学方法的运用。如果说存在一个论点，那就是它简单明了：诗歌是语言，因此诗歌必须纳入语言学的范畴；“任何研究语言的语言学家都可以而且必须将诗歌纳入其研究范围”（第377页，斜体为笔者所加）。他赞同地引用了评论家约翰·霍兰德的观点，即“似乎没有理由试图将文学与整体语言学割裂开来”，并以此作为结尾：

The conference did not, of course, settle these matters, and there were actually three closing statements, not just Jakobson’s, as is often supposed. The closing statement on behalf of literary criticism was made by the eminent critic René Wellek, and he was deeply sceptical about the claims of the linguists. All the same, the period of dominance in literary studies by the humanistic approach of the New Critics was entering its final phase, and the prestige of linguistics was rising – the American linguist Noam Chomsky, born in 1922, and about to become as dominant a force in the linguistic thinking of his generation as Saussure had been half a century earlier, had already published his first book (Syntactic Structures, 1957), and it was discussed by some of the speakers at the conference. Using concepts drawn from linguistics would soon become almost the default way of doing theory, partly because of the enormous success of Chomsky’s work in arguing that grammar and semantics (that is, meaning) cannot be separated, and that ‘deep’ syntactical structures are the ultimate determinants of meaning.* Jakobson’s closing statement makes no attempt to sum up the arguments put forward in the course of the conference. Rather, his densely technical analyses of poetry show the linguistic method at work. The argument, if there is one, is brutal and simple: poetry is language, so poetry must now come within the sphere of linguistics; ‘the linguist whose field is any kind of language may and must include poetry in his study’ (p. 377, my italics). He moves towards his conclusion by approvingly quoting the critic John Hollander to the effect that ‘there seems to be no reason for trying to separate the literary from the overall linguistic’, and he ends with this resounding proclamation:

然而，我们所有人都清楚地认识到，对语言的诗意功能充耳不闻的语言学家，以及对语言问题漠不关心、不熟悉语言学方法的文学学者，都是同样明显的时代错位。（第377页）

All of us here, however, definitely realize that a linguist deaf to the poetic function of language and a literary scholar indifferent to linguistic problems and unconversant with linguistic methods are equally flagrant anachronisms. (p. 377)

从此以后，文学批评的首要目标是“科学”和系统化，而仅仅具备智力和文学鉴赏力已远远不够。欢迎来到后印第安纳时代的美好新世界！

Henceforth, literary criticism would strive above all to be ‘scientific’ and methodical, and mere intelligence, combined with literary sensibility, would no longer be enough. Welcome to the brave new post-Indiana world!



1966年约翰·霍普金斯大学国际研讨会

The Johns Hopkins University international

symposium, 1966

阅读：《结构主义之争》，理查德·麦克西和尤金尼奥·多纳托编，约翰·霍普金斯大学出版社，1970年（2006年四十周年纪念版）。这是“会议论文集”，收录了德里达的演讲《结构、符号与游戏》以及随后提出的问题。

Reading:The Structuralist Controversy, ed. Richard Macksey and Eugenio Donato, Johns Hopkins University Press, 1970 (fortieth anniversary edition, 2006). This is the ‘book of the conference’, containing Derrida’s lecture ‘Structure, Sign and Play’, and the questions which followed.

1966年10月，一场题为“批评的语言与人类科学”的国际研讨会在美国约翰·霍普金斯大学举行。研讨会标题的构成要素表明了语言学的持续主导地位，但此次会议的目标仍然是跨学科的。可以说，此次研讨会是与巴黎高等研究院“人类科学”系合作举办的，而该系正是结构主义的摇篮。“人类科学”这一术语标志着一个新的学科领域，它将传统意义上的人文科学和社会科学联系起来，涵盖了（除其他领域外）人类学、哲学、文学、语言学、心理学和历史学等领域。可以说，这是各个学科的交汇点，它们在结构主义的庇护下汇聚了资源。本次研讨会庆祝了结构主义的到来和确立，其主要人物——勒内·吉拉尔、乔治·普莱、吕西安·戈德曼、茨维坦·托多罗夫和罗兰·巴特——都发表了文章。结构主义的巩固可以被视为超越语言学完全主导地位的一次进步，因为人们现在意识到，语言学无法真正兑现其“为理解所有人类现象提供普遍框架”（第xi页）的承诺。因此，形势再次发生变化，德里达的贡献在于表明了他对结构主义胜利的怀疑，并开启了“后结构主义”的新阶段。

In October 1966 an international symposium was held at Johns Hopkins University in the USA under the title ‘The Languages of Criticism and the Sciences of Man’. The sequence of elements in the title of the symposium indicates the on-going primacy of linguistics, but again the aim of the gathering was to be interdisciplinary. The symposium was a co-production, so to speak, with the ‘Sciences de l’Homme’ section of the Ecole des Hautes Etudes, Paris, which was the cradle of structuralism. This term ‘the sciences of man’ indicated a new subject area which linked the interests of what would more conventionally have been called the Humanities and the Social Sciences, taking in (among other areas) anthropology, philosophy, literature, linguistics, psychology and history. This is the nexus of disciplines which, so to speak, had pooled resources under the aegis of structuralism, and this symposium celebrated the arrival and establishment of structuralism, with contributions from its major figures – René Girard, Georges Poulet, Lucien Goldmann, Tzvetan Todorov and Roland Barthes. This consolidation of structuralism can be seen as a move forward and beyond the complete dominance of linguistics, for it was now realised that linguistics could not really deliver on its promise to provide ‘a universal matrix for understanding all human phenomena’ (p. xi). Hence, the ground was shifting again, and the impact of Derrida’s contribution was to announce his scepticism about the structuralist triumph and to inaugurate a new stage of ‘post-structuralism’.

德里达演讲的内容在第三章中有详细描述。现在让我印象深刻的是，就像大多数会议上令人难忘的重要发言一样，它几乎不关注周围的论点或语境，只是以饱满的热情和坚定的信念抛出自己的挑战。但他的方法中固有的弱点和优点也已经显露出来。在德里达对问题的回应中（参见其论文后的“讨论”，第265-272页），让·伊波利特（Jean Hyppolite）对他进行了持续的追问。伊波利特的问题源于结构主义视角——没有指称对象，结构还能存在吗？我们思想中先前的“中心”（例如“人”、“上帝”、“真理”等概念）已被“去中心化”并抹去，取而代之的是诸如“差异”之类的结构，也就是说，我们既没有A也没有B，我们只有它们之间的差异。例如，语言是一种游戏，它有一套规则结构，但我们不会去探究这游戏的目的是什么，或者它最终服务于什么目的。因此，伊波利特想知道德里达认为语言结构背后是什么——“没有中心，就无法思考结构”，他说（266）。为了理解他的意思，不妨想想一场足球比赛。这项赛事有着一套错综复杂的规则和惯例，但规则背后究竟是什么？是比赛或观赛带来的兴奋感吗？是获胜队伍获得的奖杯吗？是胜利的荣耀，还是胜利带来的战胜人生逆境的升华感？显然，这些结构背后必定蕴藏着某种东西，而伊波利特想知道德里达认为那是什么。但德里达当然不会告诉他，他以一种后来随着名声大噪而变得过于惯常的方式回避了这个问题——“我不知道我要去哪里，”他说（267）。当被进一步追问“结构”究竟是什么时（“你如何为我定义结构？——看看中心在哪里”，268），德里达回答说，“结构”的概念“已经不再令人满意”，因此“我所说的可以被理解为对结构主义的批判”（268）。一位提问者指责他总是谈论“非中心”，并指出如果没有中心的概念，就无法解释感知是什么，“因为感知恰恰是我眼中世界呈现中心的方式”（271）。对此，德里达否认他否认过中心的存在，但补充道：“我相信中心是一种功能，而非存在——一种现实，但是一种功能”（271）。然而，他最终还是否认了感知的存在——“我不相信存在任何类似感知的东西……我不相信存在任何感知”（272）。这似乎否定了后结构主义的“温和选项”观点，即认为它仅仅是一个强调万物建构性的系统，换句话说，感知总是包含概念这一概念。引人注目的是，质疑的过程似乎表明德里达几乎被推向了比他预期更为极端的论述，而这些论述之后将无法回头。1966年会议的资料于1971年整理成文，会议论文集最终于1972年出版。六十年代中期到七十年代初期的知识氛围发生了显著变化。到1972年，德里达对结构主义的挑战的影响逐渐显现，至少对于主要思想家而言，后结构主义时代已经全面到来。

The content of Derrida’s talk is described in Chapter 3, and what strikes me about it now is that – like most of the memorable and significant contributions at conferences – it takes very little notice of the surrounding arguments or contexts and simply bangs down its challenge with flare and conviction. But the characteristic weaknesses as well as the strengths of his approach are already apparent in Derrida’s response to questions (see ‘Discussion’ after his paper, pp. 265-72). He is questioned with some persistence by Jean Hyppolite, whose query comes from a structuralist perspective – can you have structures without a referent? The previous ‘centres’ of our thought (notions like ‘Man’, ‘God’, ‘Truth’, and so on) have been ‘de-centred’ and wiped away, and instead we are left with structures like ‘difference’, that is, we have neither A nor B, we have only the difference between them. Language, for instance, is a game, with a structure of rules, but we don’t ask what the game is for, or what ultimate end it serves. So Hyppolite wants to know what Derrida thinks is behind the structure of language – ‘One cannot think of the structure without the centre’, he says (266). To see what he is getting at, think, for instance, of a game of football. There is an intricate structure of rules and conventions which govern the event, but what is behind the rules? Is it something to do with the excitement of playing or watching the game? Is it the cup which the winning team receives? Is it the glory of victory, or the sublimated sense which winning gives of triumphing over the adversities of life? Obviously, there must be something behind the structures, and Hyppolite wants to know what Derrida thinks it is. But of course, Derrida doesn’t tell him, and the question is deflected in ways which later became all too automatic for Derrida as his fame grew – ‘I do not know where I am going,’ he says (267). Pressed further to say what structure is (‘how will you define a structure for me? – to see where the centre is’, p. 268), Derrida replies that the concept of structure ‘is no longer satisfactory’, so ‘what I have said can be understood as a criticism of structuralism’ (268). He is accused of always speaking of ‘non-centres’ by a questioner who says that without a notion of centres you can’t explain what perception is, ‘for a perception is precisely the manner in which the world appears centred to me’ (271). In response, Derrida denies that he has denied the existence of centres, but adds, ‘I believe that the centre is a function, not a being – a reality, but a function’ (271). But he does conclude by denying the existence of perception – ‘I don’t believe that anything like perception exists … I don’t believe that there is any perception’ (272). This would seem to close off the ‘soft option’ view of post-structuralism, that is, the view that it is merely a system which emphasises the constructedness of everything, in other words, the notion that perceiving is always con ceiving. It is striking that the questioning process seems to show Derrida almost being pushed into more extreme formulations than he intended, from which it will later be impossible to pull back. The material from the 1966 conference was written up in 1971, and the book of the conference was finally published in 1972. The change in intellectual climate between the mid sixties and the early seventies was very considerable. By 1972, the implications of the Derridean challenge to structuralism were sinking in, and for the major thinkers, at least, the age of postructuralism was already in full swing.

《解构与批评》出版于1979年

The publication of Deconstruction and Criticism, 1979

阅读材料：本书本身，以及一些重要的评论，包括 SL Goldberg 在《伦敦书评》（1980 年 5 月 22 日至 6 月 4 日）和 Denis Donoghue 在《纽约书评》（1980 年 6 月 12 日）上发表的题为“解构解构”的评论，以及 Roger Scruton 于 1980 年在 BBC Radio 3 播出的演讲，该演讲被转载到他的著作《文化政治及其他论文》（Carcanet 出版社，1981 年）中。

Reading: the book itself, and a sample of key reviews, including S. L. Goldberg, London Review of Books (May 22–June 4, 1980), and Denis Donoghue, New York Review of Books (June 12, 1980), under the title ‘Deconstructing Deconstruction’, and Roger Scruton’s talk, which was broadcast on BBC Radio 3 in 1980 and is reprinted in his book The Politics of Culture and Other Essays (Carcanet, 1981).

这本书由五位作者合著，于1979年由耶鲁大学出版社出版。这五位作者分别是哈罗德·布鲁姆、保罗·德曼、雅克·德里达、杰弗里·哈特曼和J·希利斯·米勒，他们有时被统称为理论界的“耶鲁黑手党”。该书以雪莱的《生命的胜利》为例，阐释了解构主义的阅读方法，并以一种毫不妥协甚至残酷的方式呈现了这种阅读方式。它展现了解构主义（当时已被视为整个文学理论的代表）的鼎盛时期——傲慢、自信、挑衅，对许多人来说，这简直是文学研究走向奥威尔式噩梦的写照：仿佛有人要求他们想象文学批评的未来，而他们看到的却是一幅靴子永远踩在文学文本上的画面。这本书的评论者们意见两极分化，要么极力赞扬，要么毫不妥协，仿佛意识到一场关乎文学研究灵魂的决定性战役正在进行。其中最引人注目、持续时间最长的批评来自S.L.戈德堡在《伦敦书评》上的评论、丹尼斯·多诺霍在《纽约书评》上的评论，以及罗杰·斯克鲁顿在BBC广播三台的访谈。

This book – by five authors – was published by Yale University Press in 1979, the five being Harold Bloom, Paul de Man, Jacques Derrida, Geoffrey Hartman, and J. Hillis Miller, a group sometimes collectively referred to as the ‘Yale Mafia’ of theory. The book exemplified deconstructive reading with reference to Shelley’s ‘The Triumph of Life’, presenting this approach to reading in its most uncompromising and even brutal form. It showed deconstruction (which by that time was being taken as representative of literary theory as a whole) in its pomp – brash, confident, and provocative, and, for many, a kind of Orwellian nightmare of what literary studies had become, as if they had been asked to imagine the future of literary criticism, and were being shown a picture of a boot stamping on the face of a literary text for ever. The reviewers of the book were polarised, and uncompromising in either praise or blame, as if conscious that a decisive battle was being fought for the soul of literary studies. The most notable and sustained attacks on it were S. L. Goldberg’s in the London Review of Books, Denis Donoghue’s in the New York Review of Books, and Roger Scruton’s BBC Radio 3 talk.

《解构与批评》之所以引起如此轩然大波，是因为它实际上并非一部解构理论著作，而是（表面上）一部解构实践著作。如果它仅仅是一部“纯粹的”理论著作，那么其他流派的敌对学术读者（或浅尝辄止者）或许会认为它与他们阅读和阐释文学的核心工作无关。如此一来，它便可能被束之高阁，沦为众多只与理论家对话、纯粹在哲学思想领域展开辩论、与日常文学阅读和写作几乎毫无关联的书籍之一。然而事实并非如此，这本书引发的冒犯和愤怒源于它似乎侵入了“文学”（借用一个传统但如今已略显过时的文学研究术语）这一人文空间，并威胁要从内部将这一领域改造成某种异类。人们非常担心这种思维方式，凭借其晦涩的词汇和抽象的表述，会对年轻的学者产生特别大的吸引力，一旦流行起来，文学研究的未来将会受到毒害。至少在英国，文学研究首次开始出现在广播和电视节目中，并以这本书为例，来探讨当时英语系发生的种种怪事。消息不胫而走，称一场“战争”正在全国各地的英语系爆发。“理论战争”一词在20世纪80年代初的人文学科讨论中迅速流行起来，《解构与批评》的出版可以被视为新晋理论家们向文学研究领域混乱的现状宣战。

Deconstruction and Criticism caused such outrage because it wasn’t in fact a work of deconstructive theory, but (ostensibly) of deconstructive practice. Had it been ‘mere’ theory, hostile academic readers (or dippers-in) of other persuasions could have dismissed it as not really being germane to their own core business of reading and interpreting literature. It could then have been brushed aside as just one more of the increasing number of books which spoke only to other theorists and carried on a debate purely in the realm of philosophical ideas, with little evident relevance to the day-to-day business of reading and writing about literature. But this was not the situation, and the feelings of affront and outrage which the book provoked came about because it seemed to have invaded the humane space of ‘letters’ (to use a traditional but now antique term for literary study), threatening to transform the field from within into something alien. There was great fear that this kind of thinking, with its arcane vocabulary and its abstract formulations, was particularly appealing to young academics, so that the future of literary study would be poisoned if it caught on. For the first time (in the UK, at least) literary studies began to be discussed on radio and TV, using this book as an example of the strange events which were taking place in English departments. Word got out that a ‘war’ of some kind was going in English faculties across the land. The term ‘the theory wars’ quickly became current in discussions of the Humanities in the early 1980s, and the publication of Deconstruction and Criticism can be seen as the declaration of war by the newly empowered theorists on the disorganised status quo in literary studies.

1981年麦凯布事件

The MacCabe affair, 1981

阅读：目前尚无关于此事件的正式学术记载，但可参阅 1980 年末至 1981 年初的报纸报道（您可在大多数大学图书馆使用《泰晤士报》全文数据库，并在 1980 年和 1981 年期间搜索“Colin MacCabe”找到这些报道），最早可参阅1981 年 1 月 24 日星期六的《泰晤士报》和1 月 25 日星期日的《星期日泰晤士报》。

Reading: No formal academic account of this event exists, but see the newspaper reports from late 1980 and early 1981 (which you can find in most university libraries by using the Times Full-text Database and searching for ‘Colin MacCabe’ in the period 1980 and 1981), beginning with the Times of Saturday 24 January 1981, and the Sunday Times of Sunday 25 January.

关于解构主义和批评的争论还未平息，1980年秋天，剑桥大学就做出了如下决定：一位名叫科林·麦凯布的年轻助理讲师在担任了五年临时教职后，未能获得正式讲师职位。学生们对此表示抗议，而做出这一决定的学院委员会内部也出现了分歧和分裂。此事被报纸报道，并在1981年上半年成为英国的热门新闻。由此引发了一场关于大学英语教学方式的公开辩论，英语系的一些知名人士也公开表明了立场。雷蒙德·威廉姆斯和弗兰克·克莫德支持麦凯布（前者欣赏他作品中的马克思主义元素，后者则欣赏其结构主义成分），而克里斯托弗·里克斯则反对麦凯布的任命，并倾向于更传统的学术方法。1981年1月24日星期六，《泰晤士报》刊登了一篇新闻报道和一篇社论，试图向读者解释什么是结构主义：“结构主义可以简单地描述为一种语言学方法，它研究语言本身如何影响作者的写作方式”，文章如此解释，但并没有提供多少帮助。这位领导者对整个体系抱持着一种非常高远的看法（“学者们争论就像孩子打闹，是为了锻炼和锻炼自己的能力”），他也认为结构主义主要关乎语言学：“结构主义首先关注的是语法——不是学校里曾经教授的那种规范意义上的语法（现在似乎已经不再教授了），而是作为语言潜意识形式，进而作为人类思维模式的语法。”在1981年提出这种观点显得非常不合时宜，因为它似乎没有意识到结构主义早已被后结构主义所取代。记者们被告知的关键人物是结构主义的奠基人——列维-斯特劳斯、罗兰·巴特等等——而不是拉康和德里达，而且完全没有提及文学理论的主流已经从语言学转向了哲学和解构主义。在我看来，关于语法和人类潜意识模式的评论，与其说是对20世纪80年代文学理论现状的描述，不如说是对乔姆斯基“深层句法”概念的阐述。文章部分内容基于记者伊恩·杰克匆匆对科林·麦凯布的采访。杰克在希思罗机场偶遇刚从英国文化协会返回的麦凯布。伊恩·杰克在麦凯布前往欧洲进行讲学的途中，于前往伦敦的出租车上对他进行了采访。采访内容于次日（1月25日）发表在《星期日泰晤士报》上，文中再次强调了语言的重要性——麦凯布在出租车上不停地“强调英国文学学生必须掌握语法”，杰克告诉读者，麦凯布感叹他的学生似乎不再接受学校语法教育，这使得他们难以传达建立在语法框架之上的观点。伊恩·杰克显然对麦凯布这样一位激进的左翼人士竟然会哀叹学校正规语法教学的衰落感到困惑不解。

The fuss about Deconstruction and Criticism was hardly over, when, in the autumn of 1980, it was decided at Cambridge University that a young assistant lecturer called Colin MacCabe would not be upgraded to a permanent lectureship, after holding a temporary post for five years. Students protested, and there were disagreements and divisions on the Faculty Board which had made the decision. The events were reported in the newspapers and became a running news story in the UK during the first half of 1981. The result was a public argument about how English should be taught at universities, with eminent figures from the English Faculty publicly taking sides. Raymond Williams and Frank Kermode supported MacCabe (the former liking the Marxist aspects of his work, and the latter the structuralist elements), while Christopher Ricks opposed MacCabe’s appointment and favoured more traditional scholarly and traditional methods. On Saturday 24 January 1981 the Times had a news article and a leader on the matter, the article struggling to explain to its readers what structuralism is: ‘Structuralism can be described simply as a linguistics technique which studies how language itself influences the way an author writes’, it informed us, not very helpfully. The leader took a very lofty view of the whole business (‘Dons dispute as children squabble, to test out and develop their muscles’), and it too saw structuralism as being primarily about linguistics: ‘Structuralism is first of all about grammar – not grammar conceived in the prescriptive sense in which it was once taught in schools (and seems to be no longer), but grammar as a pattern of the subliminal forms of language, and therefore of the human mind’. This is a very anachronistic note to strike as late as 1981, for it seems to be unaware that structuralism had now long been replaced by post-structuralism, but the key names the reporters were told about were those of the structuralist founding fathers – Levi-Strauss, Roland Barthes, and so on – rather than Lacan and Derrida, and there is no mention of the fact that the tune in literary theory was now being called by philosophy and deconstruction rather than linguistics. The comments on grammar and the subliminal patterns of the human mind seem to me more like a description of Chomsky’s idea of ‘deep syntax’ than the state of literary theory in the 1980s. The leader was partly based on an interview with Colin MacCabe which had been hurriedly conducted by journalist Ian Jack. He met MacCabe at Heathrow Airport, on his return from a British Council lecturing trip to Europe, and interviewed him during the taxi ride into London. The interview was published in the Sunday Times the next day (25 January), and again the emphasis on language is very marked – MacCabe in the taxi kept ‘banging on about the need of Eng. Lit. students to know grammar’, and Jack tells his readers that MacCabe laments the fact that his students no longer seem to have been taught grammar at school, making it difficult to convey ideas which build upon that framework. Ian Jack was evidently puzzled to hear a lament about the decline of formal grammar teaching in schools coming from a radical left-winger like MacCabe.

这场争论在剑桥持续发酵，似乎演变成了一场闹剧，就像汤姆·夏普1974年的讽刺小说《波特豪斯蓝调》（讲述的是虚构的剑桥学院里保守派和改革派之间的斗争）中的某个情节。此时，人事任命委员会的会议记录已被泄露，校方宣布将由“大学古老的七人法庭”（ Septem Viri）对泄密事件展开调查。随后，学生们发起反抗，对学院委员会投出了不信任票，要求对英语系的现状进行公开调查。调查在参议院大楼举行，报纸报道中不出所料地将其描述为“橡木镶板”。这本应是一场结构主义者、马克思主义者、人文主义者和其他学者之间的高水平学术辩论，但结果却并非如此——它只关乎程序、行政管理和委员会运作。当时的高等教育正迅速发展，但撒切尔政府却严格削减经费——校舍破败不堪，清洁工短缺，学生们抱怨与导师的接触时间不足，而导师们也越来越迫于压力，不得不加快科研步伐。最终，这场“风波”不了了之：双方达成妥协，麦凯布的职位得以延长一年，但他在1981年7月离开剑桥，接受了格拉斯哥斯特拉斯克莱德大学的教授职位。总的来说，理论学界从这场风波中受益匪浅：一位才华横溢、思想前卫的年轻人，其职业生涯正受到保守势力的威胁。我们可以说，理论学界如今有了它的殉道者，也更加意识到自身的内在逻辑和重要性。

The dispute dragged on at Cambridge and seemed to descend into farcical parody, like an episode in Tom Sharpe’s 1974 satirical novel Porterhouse Blue (which is about the struggle between reactionaries and reformers at a mythical Cambridge college). The proceedings of the appointments committee had by now been leaked, and it was announced that the leak would be investigated ‘by the university’s ancient court the Septem Viri’ (the Seven Men). Then the students revolted and passed a vote of no confidence in the Faculty Board, calling for an open enquiry into the state of the English Faculty. This duly took place in the Senate House, inevitably described in the newspaper reports as ‘oak-panelled’. It should have been a high-level intellectual debate between structuralists, Marxists, humanists, and the rest, but of course it wasn’t – it was about procedures, and administration, and committees. Higher education in those days was expanding rapidly, but funding was being rigorously curtailed by the Thatcher government – there was wet rot in buildings and a lack of cleaners, and students complained about inadequate contact time with tutors who were increasingly being pressured to get on with their research. The ‘affair’, in the end, fizzled out: a compromise was reached whereby MacCabe’s post would be extended for a further year, but in July 1981 he left Cambridge to take up the offer of a professorship at the enterprising Strathclyde University in Glasgow. On the whole, theory benefited from all this publicity: here, it seemed, was a bright young talent with cutting-edge ideas whose career was being threatened by the forces of reaction. Theory, we might say, now had its martyr, and an increased sense of its own coherence and importance.

伊格尔顿的《文学理论

导论》出版于1983年

The publication of Eagleton’s Literary Theory:

An Introduction, 1983

阅读：本书本身，以及约翰·贝利在《泰晤士报文学副刊》（1983 年 6 月 10 日）上发表的早期评论。

Reading: the book itself, and early reviews such as John Bayley’s in the Times Literary Supplement (10 June 1983).

回顾20世纪70年代以来文学理论的传播，似乎势不可挡，但实际上，它取决于找到有效的理论教学方法，而不仅仅是在本科和研究生阶段学习理论的方法。麦凯布事件凸显了这方面的一些困难，并表明了详细阐述、例证和讨论的必要性。当时大多数文学理论的原始文献都是用法语写成的，少数是用德语或俄语写成的，而且远非全部都有译本。因此，迫切需要一些“中介”作品，即可以作为本科生和硕士生课程教材的入门书籍。如果没有这类书籍，文学理论注定只能是少数精英的兴趣。1977年，梅休恩出版社（Methuen）出版了“新视角”（New Accents）系列丛书，首次满足了对基础性二级阐释的需求。该系列丛书为学生提供了关于结构主义、解构主义、后结构主义等方面的入门书籍。对文学理论进行入门概述也势在必行，而第一本满足这一需求的书籍是特里·伊格尔顿（Terry Eagleton）的《文学理论导论》（Literary Theory: An Introduction），由布莱克威尔出版社（Blackwell）于1983年出版。这本书一经问世便大获成功，因为它文笔生动活泼、引人深思，并且避免了写成晦涩难懂的巨著——这样的书或许能让同行们印象深刻，但对于寻求入门启迪的学生来说却并不合适。这些特点使它区别于后来的大多数同类书籍，也区别于从20世纪80年代末开始涌现的文学理论教材。收录众多重要人物的关键文章和章节的“读本”，如果经过精心挑选并努力满足用户的实际需求，将会非常有用。但是，这类书籍很久以前就屈服于竞争性的超大篇幅，出版公司之间展开了一场荒谬的扑克游戏，看谁能出版篇幅最长的理论读本（出版社 N 对出版社 B 说：“我看到你的 1300 页，然后我再加 1300 页”）。

The spread of literary theory since the 1970s seems in retrospect to have been inevitable and relentless, but in reality it was dependent upon finding effective ways of teaching theory, not just ways of studying it at faculty and postgraduate level. The MacCabe affair highlighted some of the difficulties of doing this and showed the need for detailed exposition, exemplification and discussion. Most of the primary texts of literary theory had been written in French, with a few in German or Russian, and by no means all of them had yet been translated. There was an acute need for ‘mediating’ works, that is, introductory books which could be used as course textbooks on undergraduate and MA courses. Without such books, literary theory would be doomed to remain an elitist minority interest. The need for basic secondary exposition was first supplied by the founding in 1977 of the series of books known as ‘Methuen New Accents’, which provided students with individual introductory books on structuralism, deconstruction, post-structuralism and the rest. An introductory overview of literary theory was also a necessity, and the first book to meet this need was Terry Eagleton’s Literary Theory: An Introduction, published by Blackwell in 1983. The book was an instant success because it was written in a lively and provocative manner, and resisted the temptation to produce a dense and elephantine tome – such a book might have impressed peers but would have been inappropriate for students seeking initial enlightenment. These qualities distinguished it from most of its successors, and from the course-book ‘readers’ in literary theory which began to appear from the late 1980s onwards. ‘Readers’ containing key articles and chapters by a range of major figures can be very useful if they are selective and if they try to meet the actual needs of their users, but such books succumbed long ago to competitive super-sizing, with publishing firms striving with each other in a ridiculous poker game to see who can produce the biggest theory reader (Publisher N to Publisher B: ‘I’ll see your thirteen hundred pages and raise you by another thirteen hundred’).

相比之下，伊格尔顿则采取了更为简洁的论述方式：他的引言题为“何为文学？”，第一章讲述了英国研究的兴起史；接下来的四章依次探讨了现象学、结构主义、后结构主义和精神分析，结论部分则题为“政治批评”。伊格尔顿毫不掩饰自己的中立立场——他是一位立场鲜明、立场明确的马克思主义批评家，而非浅尝辄止地浅尝辄止地涉猎各种“主义”，对每一种“主义”浅尝辄止，然后就转向下一种。书中的一些遗漏也颇为引人注目——例如，索引（本书出版于1983年）中竟然没有“女权主义”或“女权主义理论”的条目，而且（在一本名为《文学理论》的书中）以“何为文学？”而非“何为文学理论？”作为开篇，似乎也有些古怪。总的来说，本书的论证有力而又艰涩：对于“何为文学？”这个问题，答案尚不明确。文学“并不像昆虫那样存在”。有人可能会不耐烦地反驳说，文学理论肯定存在，甚至可能像昆虫那样存在，因为伊格尔顿就写过一本关于文学理论的书。但对伊格尔顿而言，文学理论的目的似乎是反文学的，这使它区别于文学批评——后者通常（人们会认为）站在文学一边。在他看来，理论如同昆虫一般，其目的似乎是扮演一种超级细菌的角色，从内部攻击文学，最终导致其消亡（但如果文学不存在，它又如何消亡呢？）。这正是伊格尔顿著名的寓言式结尾所提出的那种神学问题：

Eagleton, by contrast, kept it simple: his introduction is called ‘What is Literature?’ and the first chapter tells the history of the rise of English Studies; the next four chapters deal in turn with phenomenology, structuralism, post-structuralism, and psychoanalysis, and the Conclusion is entitled ‘Political Criticism’. Eagleton makes no pretence to neutrality – he is a Marxist critic writing from a committed and identified position, not a sipper and taster of ‘isms’ who swills each one round for a few moments and then passes on to the next one. The omissions are striking – the index (this is in 1983) has no entry on ‘feminism’ or ‘feminist theory’, for instance, and it seems somewhat eccentric (in a book called Literary Theory) to begin by asking ‘What is Literature?’ rather than ‘What is Literary Theory?’ The overall argument is vigorous but taxing: the answer to the question ‘What is Literature?’ is that literature ‘does not exist in the sense that insects do’. It might be retorted impatiently that literary theory must certainly exist, possibly even in the sense that insects do, since Eagleton has written a book about it. But literary theory’s purpose, for Eagleton, seems anti-literary, and that distinguishes it from literary criticism, which is usually (one would presume) on literature’s side. For him, theory’s insect-like purpose seems to be to act as a kind of super-bug, attacking literature from within, with the aim of bringing about its death (though if literature doesn’t exist, how can it die?). That is the kind of theological question which is posed by Eagleton’s famous allegorical ending:

最后，我想用一个寓言来结束。我们都知道狮子比驯狮人强大，驯狮人也知道这一点。问题在于，狮子自己并不知道。文学的消亡或许能唤醒这头狮子，这并非不可能。

I shall end with an allegory. We know that the lion is stronger than the lion-tamer, and so does the lion-tamer. The problem is that the lion does not know it. It is not out of the question that the death of literature may help the lion to awaken.

正如约翰·贝利在1983年6月10日《泰晤士报文学副刊》的评论中所说，问题是“狮子是什么？” 想必，狮子是无产阶级，而驯狮者是文学。因此，理论的任务是反对文学，剥夺其征服和安抚群众的力量。然而，伊格尔顿笔下的狮子似乎比他自己认为的更有智慧，因为它知道驯狮者手握鞭子，而这正是驯狮者比狮子更强大的原因。这个比喻必须将文学视为鞭子，将其视为“意识形态国家机器”的一部分，这台机器通过意识形态而非武力来控制我们（参见第八章）。（阿尔都塞的“ISA”概念）。伊格尔顿著作的力量和影响力在于其整体的活力、机智和思维敏捷，以及对大量思想的精辟概括。例如，他在关于结构主义的章节中，论述精炼而又信息丰富；在关于后结构主义的章节中，他提出了其他人十多年后才开始探讨的问题；关于精神分析的章节则较为常规；而他关于政治批评的最后一章则毫不妥协地展现了他的马克思主义立场，但同时也预示了他二十年后将要关注的伦理和道德问题——他指出，“成为一个‘更好的人’意味着什么，必须是具体而实际的”。因此，伊格尔顿的著作极大地促进了文学理论的“巩固”，并帮助其在本科课程中站稳脚跟，使教师们相信系统地教授文学理论是可行的。在这段包含十个事件的历史中，它标志着理论兴起的顶峰。

As John Bayley said in his Times Literary Supplement review (10 June 1983), the question is ‘What is the lion?’ Presumably, the lion is the proletariat, and the lion-tamer is literature. So the job of theory is to oppose literature and deprive it of its power to subdue and pacify the masses. Eagleton’s lion, however, seems wiser than he allows, for the lion knows that the lion-tamer has a whip, and that is what makes him stronger than the lion. The metaphor must envisage literature as the whip, seeing it as part of the ‘Ideological State Apparatus’, which controls us by ideology rather than force (see Chapter 8 for the Althusserian notion of the ‘ISA’). The power and impact of Eagleton’s book lay in its overall energy, wit, and mental agility, and in its deft summaries of large bodies of thought. He is brilliantly compressed and informative, for instance, in his chapter on structuralism; in the chapter on post-structuralism he raises the issues that others only got round to more than a decade later; the psychoanalysis chapter is more routine, and his final chapter on political criticism puts his Marxist cards uncompromisingly face-up on the table, but in a way that anticipates the ethical and moral issues which would pre-occupy him twenty years later – ‘What it means to be a “better person”’, he says, ‘must be concrete and practical’. Eagle-ton’s book, then, greatly contributed to the ‘consolidation’ of literary theory and helped to establish it firmly on the undergraduate curriculum, giving tutors confidence that it might be possible to teach it in a systematic way. In this ten-event history it marks the apex of the rise of theory.

J·希利斯·米勒的省议员主席致辞，1986年

J. Hillis Miller’s MLA presidential address, 1986

阅读： '1986 年总统致辞。理论的胜利、对阅读的抵制以及物质基础的问题。' PMLA（1987 年 5 月），102(3): 281–91；新历史主义者路易斯·蒙特罗斯的回应，'宣扬文艺复兴：文化的诗学和政治学'，转载于 Rivkin & Ryan，第 777–85 页。

Reading: ‘Presidential Address, 1986. The Triumph of Theory, the Resistance to Reading, and the Question of the Material Base.’ PMLA (May 1987), 102(3): 281–91; response by New Historicist Louis Montrose, ‘Professing the Renaissance: The Poetics and Politics of Culture’, reprinted in Rivkin & Ryan, pp. 777–85.

到了20世纪80年代中期，文学理论即将衰落的迹象开始显现。一个关键时刻是1986年J·希利斯·米勒在现代语言协会（MLA）的主席致辞。MLA是美国大学英语教师的主要专业机构，其年会是该学科的重大盛事。主席的主题演讲是大会的高潮，通常以“学科现状”宣言的形式出现，并会指出未来的发展方向。希利斯·米勒作为“解构主义与批评”的“五大著名”作者之一，长期以来一直是解构主义的拥护者。他的演讲表明，他曾预期20世纪80年代初期的强劲势头——当时解构主义似乎正在席卷美国各大知名英语系——将会延续下去。然而，实际情况似乎是，解构主义的主导地位正在逐渐瓦解。理论正受到一股新的反作用力的制约。这股反作用力源于早期现代主义研究领域，并在美国由斯蒂芬·格林布拉特的《文艺复兴时期的自我塑造》（1980）和英国由乔纳森·多利莫尔和艾伦·辛菲尔德的《政治莎士比亚》（1985）开创（参见第九章）。正如希利斯·米勒所认识到的，历史主义与解构主义截然相反，而解构主义在20世纪80年代已成为理论本身最突出的公共体现，取代了结构主义在70年代的地位。因此，米勒指出，（实际上）“理论的胜利”正被令人遗憾的历史主义浪潮所打断：

By the mid 1980s, symptoms of the coming decline of literary theory began to emerge. A key moment was the Modern Language Association’s presidential address by J. Hillis Miller in 1986. The MLA is the main professional body for university teachers of English in the USA, and its annual conventions are major events for the discipline. The keynote address from the president is the climax, and it takes the form of a kind of ‘state of the discipline’ pronouncement which will often point to future lines of development. Hillis Miller, as one of the ‘famous five’ authors of Deconstruction and Criticism, had long been a proponent of deconstruction, and his address shows that he had expected that the confident momentum of the early 1980s – when deconstruction seemed to be making a clean sweep of prestigious English departments in the USA – would continue. However, what was actually happening, it seemed, was that the dominance of theory was being checked by a new contrary force. The contrary force was the rise of historicist approaches to literature, emanating from the field of early modernist studies, and begun in the USA by Stephen Greenblatt’s Renaissance Self-Fashioning (1980) and in the UK by Jonathan Dollimore and Alan Sinfield’s Political Shakespeare in 1985 (see Chapter 9). Historicism, as Hillis Miller realised, is the polar opposite of deconstruction, which had become the most prominent public embodiment of theory itself in the 80s, taking over the status which structuralism had had in the 70s. So Miller noted that (in effect) the ‘Triumph of Theory’ was being interrupted by regrettable outbreaks of historicism:

近几年来，文学研究几乎普遍地从以语言本身为导向的理论转向了历史、文化、社会、政治、制度、阶级和性别状况、社会背景以及物质基础。（第283页）

Literary study in the past few years has undergone a sudden, almost universal turn away from theory in the sense of an orientation toward language as such and has made a corresponding turn toward history, culture, society, politics, institutions, class and gender conditions, the social context, the material base. (p. 283)

历史主义（区别于历史本身）是那些厌倦了理论的学术大众（主要是）转向的方向，而且是转向更为精细复杂的形式，这涉及到大量的档案工作、建立跨学科研究中心以及开展跨机构合作。正如他所阐述的那样，许多人选择希利斯·米勒所不赞同的一方，原因似乎显而易见，因为“历史、文化、社会、政治、制度、阶级和性别状况、社会背景、物质基础”作为研究领域，听起来比（正如米勒所说）“对语言本身的取向”更有趣。本质上，解构主义文学理论认为，学生应该研究“文学性”本身，而不是文学作品（也就是说，研究意义的概念化过程，而不是例如《米德尔马契》的具体意义）。实际上，将“文学性本身”这一概念转化为可行的本科课程一直非常困难，而那些鸿篇巨制的文学理论“读本”恰恰证明了这一点。同样，在文学研究中追求“对语言本身的取向”有点像直视太阳——你无法长时间盯着它，它会损害你的健康，而且你很快就会想要把目光转向别处。研究历史、文化、性别状况等等则要具体得多，而翻译……将如此广泛的兴趣融入学生乐于学习的课程体系并非难事。因此，解构主义转向历史主义的趋势其实并不令人意外。

Historicism (as distinct from history) is what the theory-weary academic masses (in the main) moved on to, and to ever more elaborate forms of it, entailing extensive archival work, the setting up of interdisciplinary research centres, and the pursuit of cross-institutional collaborations. As he presents the choice, it might seem rather obvious why many were choosing the side that Hillis Miller disapproved of, for ‘history, culture, society, politics, institutions, class and gender conditions, the social context, the material base’ sound rather more interesting as a field of study than (as Miller phrased it) ‘an orientation toward language as such’. Essentially, deconstructive literary theory believed that students should study ‘literariness’ itself, rather than literature (that is, the process of the conceptualisation of meaning in general, rather than the specific meanings of, for example, Middlemarch). In practice, it has always been very difficult to translate this notion of ‘literariness itself’ into a viable undergraduate curriculum, and all those elephantine literary theory ‘readers’ merely demonstrate that this is so. Likewise, striving for ‘an orientation towards language as such’ is a bit like trying to look at the sun in literary studies – you can’t do it for long, it can be damaging, and you very quickly want to look elsewhere. Studying history, culture, gender conditions, and the rest, is much more concrete, and translating that range of interests into a syllabus which students would want to follow isn’t such a difficult task. So the turning of the tide away from deconstruction and towards historicism was not really a surprising trend.

但我们此时需要探究的，究竟是历史主义与历史之间的区别是什么？历史学家或许会通过严谨的研究来重现过去，让我们仿佛置身于莎士比亚时代的伦敦街头，前往剧院观看《哈姆雷特》。我们会知道当时的街道是什么样子，闻到当时的气味，听到当时的喧嚣，甚至知道需要多少硬币才能进入剧院。（当然，这只是乔伊斯《尤利西斯》中“斯库拉与卡律布狄斯”一节里斯蒂芬的幻想。）请注意，这些都是外在的、物质性的事物，代表了历史研究所揭示的内容。此类探究的最终目标或许是伦敦的南岸环球剧院（Bankside Globe），这是一座尽可能还原伊丽莎白时代风貌的剧院，如今我们可以前往那里，体验一番类似的感受：像当时的底层观众一样站在露天剧场，甚至如果观看的是“古英语”（Old Pronunciation）版本，还能听到伊丽莎白时代人们听到的英语发音（当然，你得能够忽略希思罗机场飞机起降的持续噪音）。但历史学家们并不喜欢像南岸环球剧院这样的项目，因为归根结底，这些外在的、物质的东西并非他们的目标。历史学家们关注的是内在的东西。他们与其说是关心伊丽莎白时代的人在剧院里看到了什么，不如说是关心观看伊丽莎白时代的人所看到的景象会有什么感受。他们也对我们所谓的“身份认同”感兴趣——包括“早期现代身份认同”、“性别身份认同”和“民族身份认同”——也就是说，他们关注的并非仅仅是外在的物质事物，而是更深层次的、渗透或超越时代物质结构的东西。“谁会在乎，”我仿佛听到他们在说，“伊丽莎白时代的人穿什么样的衬衫，或者他们怎么发音英语——我想了解的是，身为伊丽莎白时代的人是什么感觉。”因此，历史学家主要关注的是“话语”、“情感结构”、“思维模式”和“身份认同”，而且在我看来，他们似乎比“真正的”历史学家更有信心，认为过去这些根本却又无形的要素是可以重现的。与历史学家不同，历史学家希望直击“身份认同”层面，而无需像历史学家那样进行枯燥乏味的考古挖掘工作。他们大部分时间都花在实践上。“历史学家总是唯物主义者，历史主义者总是唯心主义者”，正如莫里斯·扎普（大卫·洛奇小说中的文学理论家英雄）所说。我认为，希利斯·米勒在他的演讲中忽略了历史学家和历史主义者之间的区别，他将历史主义的对立力量仅仅视为一种格拉德格林式的对事实的兴趣，他自然无法理解这种兴趣如何能与“语言本身”的魅力相媲美。因此，在我看来，第六次事件标志着理论的巨大而迅速的成功开始滋生某种自满情绪。它在英国和美国享有盛誉的机构中产生的巨大影响，使其既低估了其他方法的吸引力，又高估了自身思想的理论寿命。

But what exactly, we need to ask at this point, is the difference between historicism and history? Well, a historian might seek through diligent research to recover the past, and enable us to walk again the streets of Shakespeare’s London, making for the playhouse to see a performance of Hamlet. We will know how the streets looked, smell the smells, hear the sounds, and know what coins exactly we need to have in our hands in order to get into the theatre.
